must_fix.title: Dialog fails to move focus inside on open when the first focusable candidate can't take focus (hidden input, control in a disabled fieldset)
must_fix.evidence: src/Dialog.tsx:25-28 getFocusable keeps <input type="hidden"> and <fieldset disabled> descendants; the open effect focuses only getFocusable(dialog)[0] with no fallback to the dialog. Probe <Dialog open title="T"><form><input type="hidden" .../><input aria-label="name"/><button>Save</button></form></Dialog> printed 'initial focus: <body>...' and after user.tab() 'after tab: <button>outside</button>'; with <fieldset disabled><button>A</button></fieldset><button>B</button> it printed 'fieldset initial: <body>...'. Breaks the issue's 'moves focus inside when it opens and traps it there'.

must_fix.title: Dialog focus trap can be escaped: nothing brings focus back once it leaves the dialog
must_fix.evidence: Tab, Shift+Tab and Escape are only handled in the dialog element's onKeyDown (src/Dialog.tsx:73-89), with no focusin/document-level containment. Probe: press on [data-backdrop], release on role=dialog (correctly no close: onOpenChange calls []), activeElement is <body>, then user.tab() printed 'after tab: <button>outside</button>'. Escape also no longer closes the dialog in that state.

nits: Test describe names reference spec labels like (C1), (G5), '(keyboard, item 5)' that are not in the repo
tests/Tabs.test.tsx hand-declares a `process` type to read README.md instead of adding @types/node
Dialog uses `description ?` so a valid ReactNode of 0 is dropped and aria-describedby omitted; `!= null` would keep it
FOCUSABLE selector omits summary, audio/video[controls] and [contenteditable=""]
Tab arrow/Home/End handling ignores modifier keys (e.g. Alt+ArrowLeft is captured)

report:
I wouldn't merge this yet. `pnpm test` passes (113 tests in 3 files) and `pnpm typecheck` is clean. Tabs and Combobox did what the issue asks in the cases I tried. The problem is the Dialog's focus handling, which fails in three common situations.

I probed each case with a temporary vitest file under `tests/__probe/` and then deleted it; `git status` is back to exactly how I found it.

**1. Dialog doesn't move focus inside when the first focusable element can't take focus.** `getFocusable` (`src/Dialog.tsx:25-28`) builds its list from a selector that includes `input` and `button`. It filters out only `tabIndex < 0`, a `disabled` attribute, and `[hidden]`/`[inert]` ancestors. That leaves `<input type="hidden">` and controls inside a `<fieldset disabled>` in the list. On open, the code calls `.focus()` on the first entry, which does nothing for these, and never falls back to the dialog itself. A form with a hidden CSRF input is the typical case.
   - `<Dialog open title="T"><form><input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="x"/><input aria-label="name"/><button>Save</button></form></Dialog>` with an `outside` button before it:
     - `initial focus: <body>...` (focus is still on the body, not inside the dialog)
     - `after tab: <button>outside</button>` (the first Tab lands outside the dialog)
   - `<Dialog open title="T"><fieldset disabled><button>A</button></fieldset><button>B</button></Dialog>` gives `fieldset initial: <body>...`
   - This breaks two requirements in the issue: "moves focus inside when it opens and traps it there".

**2. The focus trap can be escaped.** Tab, Shift+Tab and Escape are only handled by the dialog element's `onKeyDown` (`src/Dialog.tsx:73-89`). Nothing pulls focus back once it lands outside the dialog, so after that the keyboard leaves it. One mouse gesture is enough: press on the backdrop and release inside the dialog. That correctly doesn't close it, but it leaves focus on `<body>`. Repro: `user.pointer([{keys:"[MouseLeft>]",target:backdrop},{keys:"[/MouseLeft]",target:dialog}])` then `user.tab()`:
   - `after press: <body>… []` (no close, focus is on the body)
   - `after tab: <button>outside</button>`
   - Escape also stops closing the dialog in this state, because the key event never reaches the dialog element.

**Nits (not blocking):**
- Test names carry labels like `(C1)`, `(G5)` and `(keyboard, item 5)` that point to a spec that isn't in the repo.
- `tests/Tabs.test.tsx` checks the README text with a hand-written `process` declaration instead of adding `@types/node`.
- `description ? …` in Dialog drops a valid `ReactNode` of `0`. `!= null` would keep it.
- `FOCUSABLE` misses `summary`, `audio[controls]`/`video[controls]` and `[contenteditable=""]`.
- Tab arrow-key handling ignores modifier keys, so Alt+ArrowLeft is also captured.
